Afrikaans

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Dutch piemel.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

piel (plural piele, diminutive pieletjie)

  1. (informal) penis, dick, cock

Aragonese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin pellem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpjel/
  • Syllabification: piel
  • Rhymes: -el

Noun

[edit]

piel f (plural piele)

  1. skin

References

[edit]
  • Bal Palazios, Santiago (2002), “piel”, in Dizionario breu de a luenga aragonesa, Zaragoza, →ISBN

Asturian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin pellis, pellem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpjel/ [ˈpjel]
  • Rhymes: -el
  • Syllabification: piel

Noun

[edit]

piel f (plural pieles)

  1. (anatomy) skin (of a human)
    Synonym: pelleyu

Further reading

[edit]
  • “piel”, in Diccionariu de la llingua asturiana [Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Asturian), 1ª edición, Academia de la Llingua Asturiana, 2000, →ISBN
  • Xosé Lluis García Arias (2002–2004), “piel”, in Diccionario general de la lengua asturiana [General Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Spanish), Editorial Prensa Asturiana, →ISBN

Central Franconian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old High German *pīl, northern variant of pfīl (“arrow”), from Latin pīlum. As a noun, the word has been lost in the dialects and has been reintroduced as Feil from cognate German Pfeil.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /piːl/

Adverb

[edit]

piel

  1. (Ripuarian) straight up; steeply
    Hä schmieß der Ball piel en de Loff.
    He throws the ball straight up in the air.

Etymology 2

Variant of pijl.

Noun

piel m (plural pielen, diminutive pieltje n or pieletje n)

  1. (Netherlands, informal) penis

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    Inherited from Old Spanish piel, from Latin pellem.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈpjel/ [ˈpjel]
    • Audio (Spain):(file)
    • Rhymes: -el
    • Syllabification: piel

    Noun

    [edit]

    piel f (plural pieles)

    1. skin
    2. fur
      Synonyms: pelo, pelaje

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • a flor de piel
    • lobo con piel de cordero
    • no vendas la piel del oso antes de cazarlo
    • piel de foca
    • piel de gallina
    • piel de sapo
    • piel fina
    • piel roja
    • pielero

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • dérmico

    Further reading

    [edit]
